question: Which gymnast was named Sportswoman of the Year for the fourth time at the Laureus Awards?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Simone Biles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Simone Biles** was honored as the **Sportswoman of the Year** at the **Laureus World Sports Awards** held in **April 2024**. This victory marked the **fourth** time she has received this prestigious individual accolade, having previously won in **2017**, **2019**, and **2020**.
 
• The **2024** awards ceremony took place at the **Palacio de Cibeles** in **Madrid**, **Spain**, celebrating the greatest sporting achievements of the past year.
 
• Biles received the award following a historic comeback to competitive gymnastics in **2023**. After a **two-year** hiatus to focus on her mental health following the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics**, she returned to win **four gold medals** at the **World Artistic Gymnastics Championships** in **Antwerp**, **Belgium**.
 
• By winning her **fourth** Laureus Sportswoman of the Year title, **Simone Biles** joined an elite group of athletes, further solidifying her status as the most decorated gymnast in the history of the sport with a total of **37** medals across the **Olympics** and **World Championships**.
 
• The award recognizes her resilience and dominance, particularly her performance in **2023** where she became the first woman to land the **Yurchenko double pike** vault in international competition, now named the **Biles II**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Laureus World Sports Awards:**
 
 
• Established in **1999** by founding patrons **Daimler** and **Richemont**, the awards are often referred to as the "Oscars of Sports."
 
• The first ceremony was held in **2000** in **Monte Carlo**, where **Tiger Woods** and **Marion Jones** were the initial winners.
 
• The shortlists for the awards are created by a panel of over **1,000** specialized sports media members from more than **70** countries.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable 2024 Winners:**
 
 
• **Novak Djokovic** was named the **Sportsman of the Year** for a record-equaling **fifth** time, matching the feat of **Roger Federer**.
 
• **Aitana Bonmati**, the **Spanish** footballer, made history by winning the **Sportswoman of the Year** nomination and the **Team of the Year** award with the **Spain women's national football team**.
 
• **Jude Bellingham**, the **Real Madrid** and **England** midfielder, won the **Breakthrough of the Year** award for his exceptional performance in **2023**.
 
 
 
• **Competitors for Sportswoman of the Year 2024:**
 
 
• **Faith Kipyegon**: A **Kenyan** middle-distance runner who set **three** world records in **2023** in the **1,500m**, **5,000m**, and **one mile** events.
 
• **Rebeca Andrade**: A **Brazilian** gymnast who won **five** medals at the **2023 World Championships**, providing stiff competition to Biles.
 
• **Sifan Hassan**: An **Ethiopian-born Dutch** athlete who won the **London Marathon** and **Chicago Marathon** in her debut year at that distance in **2023**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Simone Biles' Career Statistics:**
 
 
• She was born on **March 14, 1997**, in **Columbus, Ohio**. At age **27**, she continues to compete at the highest level.
 
• She holds **7** Olympic medals, including **4 gold**, **1 silver**, and **2 bronze**, earned during the **Rio 2016** and **Tokyo 2020** Games.
 
• Biles has **five** skills named after her in the **Code of Points**: **two** on floor exercise, **two** on vault, and **one** on balance beam, reflecting her technical innovation in gymnastics.
 
• In **2022**, she was awarded the **Presidential Medal of Freedom** by **Joe Biden**, becoming the youngest person ever to receive the highest civilian honor in the **United States**.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Mental Health:**
 
 
• Biles is widely credited with sparking a global conversation on athlete mental health after withdrawing from several events at the **2021** Tokyo Olympics due to "**twisties**" (a psychological block).
 
• Her **2024** Laureus win serves as a validation of her decision to prioritize well-being over competition, demonstrating a successful return to peak performance.
